verdict.summary: NVIDIA remains the cleanest earnings read-through on AI infrastructure, but the stock is no longer a simple chip-cycle bet. Q2 FY27 revenue reached $96.2B, up 106% YoY, with Data Center at $89.0B, up 117%; both GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin were 75.0%. Q3 guidance of $108.0B, plus or minus 2%, assumes no China Data Center compute revenue, making export restrictions a visible downside. GAAP EPS of $2.46 exceeded non-GAAP EPS of $2.22 because investment gains boosted reported profit. The dated valuation scenario is 12.7x annualized guided revenue and only 1.8% annualized operating-cash-flow yield. The trade remains a watch: $227.46 requires a completed 15-minute close with regular-session volume; $224.50 is the structural stop, followed by the $232.2799 and $236.5399 pivots. Rubin production and networking attach can extend the cycle. A margin miss, hyperscaler digestion or tighter China controls would break it.

business.overview:
NVIDIA monetizes accelerated computing through GPUs and CPUs, high-speed networking, rack-scale systems, enterprise software and developer libraries. Data Center is a disclosed market platform and generated $89.0B in Q2 FY27; it sits inside Compute & Networking reporting rather than constituting a separate reportable segment.

The AI transmission channel is paid compute. More training, inference and agent workloads require accelerators, memory bandwidth, networking and CUDA-optimized software; Rubin and Spectrum-6 increase NVIDIA content per deployed AI factory rather than merely replacing one GPU generation.

The model breaks if customers digest capacity, shift meaningful workloads to internal ASICs, or cannot secure power and financing. China restrictions, foundry and packaging concentration, and a mistimed platform transition can turn exceptional demand into inventory and margin pressure.

NVIDIA's per-share test is shipment quality: operating cash must keep pace while receivables and inventory expand through Rubin. Equity-investment gains cannot substitute for accelerator, networking and systems profit.

Rubin execution must preserve gross margin while converting inventory and receivables into collected system revenue.
business.moat: CUDA's installed developer base, co-designed compute/networking/software stack and annual platform cadence reduce customer time-to-deployment. The moat is strongest when system performance and software availability matter more than chip price; it weakens if hyperscaler ASICs absorb standardized workloads or interoperability lowers switching costs.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: NVIDIA had about 24.15B shares outstanding in the current bundle; Q2 diluted weighted-average shares were 24.285B versus 24.532B a year earlier. The 24.285B quarterly diluted average is the minimum calculable per-share denominator, but a current theoretical fully diluted count remains unavailable because the filing does not convert every unvested award into a point-in-time total. The June 17 final 424B5 completed $25.0B of unsecured senior notes across seven series, carrying 4.250%-5.625% coupons and 2028-2056 maturities, for about $24.9B net proceeds. That transaction increased debt and refinancing capacity but issued no common equity, created no ATM and caused no direct share dilution.

filingsReview.summary: 4 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade A- measures fundamentals; trade state watch measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The July-quarter 10-Q supports $96.2B revenue, $63.1B receivables and $31.6B inventory; liquidity is ample, but working-capital concentration makes shipment conversion and customer acceptance decision-critical controls.
The earnings 8-K and Exhibit 99.1 support 106% revenue growth and $108B Q3 guidance excluding China compute; this is operating disclosure, not an ATM, common issuance or debt.

The final June 17 424B5 completed $25.0B of unsecured senior notes: $3.5B 4.250% due 2028, $3.5B 4.350% due 2029, $4.0B 4.500% due 2031, $3.5B 4.750% due 2033, $4.0B 4.950% due 2036, $3.0B 5.550% due 2046 and $3.5B 5.625% due 2056. It is debt, not equity issuance, an ATM or a secondary sale.

The June 15 preliminary 424B5 described the same seven-series senior-note transaction with amounts, coupons and pricing still blank. It established proposed debt financing only; the later final supplement supplies the completed $25.0B terms, and neither document issued common stock.

macro.impact: NVIDIA is the upstream volume and pricing signal for the AI complex. Its order conversion drives foundry, HBM, networking, server, power and data-center demand; conversely, export controls, hyperscaler capex digestion or financing constraints propagate through the entire chain before most downstream vendors report.

tradeIdea.entryNote: Single activation level $227.46 from the observed RTH opening range. Quote snapshot $226.72 at 2026-08-28T13:32:23Z. Watch $227.46: activation requires a completed 15-minute close above it with non-zero regular-session volume. Stop basis: August 14 reaction low at $224.50; a post-earnings breakout that loses this pivot has failed acceptance. TP1 basis: June 2 swing high at $232.2799, the first closed-bar resistance above activation. TP2 basis: May 14 swing high at $236.5399, the highest dated pivot in the frozen bar set.
tradeIdea.thesis: The trade requires proof that the post-earnings market will pay above $227.46 for a business guiding to $108.0B next quarter. A valid close activates risk to the $224.50 Aug. 14 pivot, with observed resistance at $232.2799 and $236.5399. Rubin shipment evidence, 75% gross-margin resilience and networking attach support continuation; China compute remains excluded from the base case, and an opening gap above the no-chase threshold voids immediate execution.
